title: Incident Keeper Runloop and Recovery Syllabus
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This page documents the Incident Keeper runloop: a compact, repeatable incident process that combines first-responder runbooks, escalation choreography, post-incident synthesis, and a game-day syllabus for safely exercising the full flow. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, responders from product teams, and on-call leads who orchestrate multi-team recoveries.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing Redwood Inference services (hosted API, model-serving runtime, routing, and status page infrastructure).
- Covers P0/P1 outages and degradations that impact SLOs, customer API availability, or data integrity.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance (handled via the maintenance playbook) and low-impact alerts routed to team queues.

Definitions

- P0: Total or near-total service outage affecting >30% of traffic or >10 customers; immediate all-hands required.
- P1: Severe degradation (latency SLO breach, high error rates, degraded throughput) that materially impacts customers.
- Incident Keeper: The role (rotating) responsible for maintaining the incident runloop timeline, ensuring comms cadence, and owning the postmortem assignment.

Incident Keeper Runloop (high-level)

1) Detect & Acknowledge (0 - 5 minutes)
   - Alerting system (Prometheus/Alertmanager -> PagerDuty) fires.
   - Primary responder must acknowledge in PagerDuty within 5 minutes. If unacknowledged, PD escalates per escalation policy to secondary.
   - Triage: collect initial scope (services impacted, region, %, major customers), set shorthand impact level (P0/P1).

2) Stabilize & Contain (5 - 30 minutes)
   - Execute specialized runbook for the symptom class (latency, 5xx spike, KV cache saturation, model OOM). See the Runbook Index section below.
   - Apply temporary mitigations with a bias toward safe rollbacks, throttling, or traffic-shedding rather than experimental fixes.

3) Communicate & Coordinate (10 - ongoing)
   - Incident Keeper opens bridge (Zoom/MS Teams/Slack DM bridge) and posts first public status if customer-facing within 15 minutes.
   - Use the status page template provided below for customer messages. Internal comm cadence: every 20 minutes until stabilization, hourly after.

4) Recover & Verify (30 minutes - 4 hours)
   - Complete rollback/fix steps, validate with smoke tests, synthetic traffic, and metrics checks.

5) Remediate & Learn (post-recovery)
   - Capture timeline, evidence, and root cause hypothesis. Assign the postmortem with owners and deadlines.

Pager thresholds and SLO triggers (reference)

| Signal | Pager threshold | SLO impact threshold | Typical escalation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 5xx rate (API service) | >5% errors for 3m | Potential SLO breach if >5m | P1 |
| Median p95 latency (gen endpoint) | p95 > 2.5s for 5m | SLO breach if >15m | P1 |
| Region availability | >10% request drop for 5m | P0 if persistent across regions | P0 |
| KV cache evictions/oom | sustained OOMs or pod restarts >2/min | P1 -> escalate to P0 if throughput collapses | P1/P0 |

Responder roles and responsibilities

- Incident Keeper (rotating): maintain timeline, own comm cadence, assign bridge operator, and ensure evidence collection.
- Primary Responder: first on the pager; executes immediate triage and first-runbook actions.
- Service Owner(s): owns rollback authority and long-term remediation tasks.
- Platform Lead: coordinates infra-level mitigations (capacity, region failover, autoscaling overrides).
- Customer Success Rep (if impacted): drafts customer-facing notes and coordinates targeted outreach to high-touch customers.

Runbook Index (quick lookup)

- api-5xx-spike: steps to identify caller, trace errors, apply temporary rate-limiting, rollback canary.
- latency-degradation-gen: validate KV cache hit-rate, model warmup, batching backpressure.
- model-kv-oom: quick steps to flush/invalidate prefix caches, reduce concurrency, and restart worker pools safely.
- routing-blackhole: DNS/service discovery validation, BGP/region failover checklist.
- storage-throttle: read/write queue inspection, circuit-breaker adjustments.

Example runbook: P0 — Total API outage (step-by-step)

Purpose: Recover API availability quickly with minimal customer data loss. Execute only under Incident Keeper coordination.

1) Immediate triage (Primary Responder)
   - Confirm alert source(s). Run:
     ```sh
     # Find recent 5xx spikes in Prometheus
     sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-proxy",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
     ```
   - Check service health page (internal): https://internal.redwood/status/ (replace with internal link)
   - Identify recent deploys in the last 60 minutes (CI pipeline): `gitlab ci list --since 60m` or check deployment-tracker.

2) Stabilize traffic
   - If deploy suspected: initiate emergency rollback to last-known-good artifact (Service Owner + Platform Lead).
   - If resource exhaustion suspected: reduce worker concurrency and enable read-only mode for non-critical endpoints. Example k8s scale command:
     ```sh
     kubectl scale deployment/api-workers --replicas=6 -n prod
     ```
   - Enable circuit-breakers at the ingress layer to reject low-value bulk requests.

3) Rapid verification
   - Run synthetic search/generation checks against canary endpoint until success rate >= 98% for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows.
   - Verify customers' top 10 keys in CloudWatch/Datadog to ensure no large tail errors remain.

4) Post-stabilization steps
   - Keep reduced blast radius configuration for 1 hour while monitoring. If stable, prepare a safe rollback/redeploy with a changelog and test matrix.
   - Escalate to P0 incident board if recovery not achieved within 60 minutes.

Escalation matrix (simplified)

| When | Who to call/notify | Channel |
|---|---|---|
| 0-10m | Primary responder -> Secondary | PagerDuty -> Slack #incidents |
| 10-30m | Incident Keeper + Platform Lead | Bridge + PagerDuty escalation |
| 30-60m | CTO on-call + Product lead | Direct call + executive notification channel |
| >60m | Executive incident bridge (SRE, Eng, Sales, CS) | Company-wide status + external comms prepared |

Evidence collection checklist (must be completed during incident)

- Timeline entries in comms channel (timestamps and short action notes).
- Prometheus graphs links for triggers (p95, error-rate, request-volume).
- Crash/oom logs, stack traces, and k8s pod restarts (kubectl get events, logs).
- Deployment hashes and commit pointers for any recent artifact.
- Synthetic test results and host-level telemetry.

Postmortem template (assign within 48 hours, due in 7 days for P0 incidents)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Date/time (start/end)
- Impact summary (customers affected, SLO impact, business impact)
- Timeline (minute-level, who did what)
- Root cause analysis (hypothesis & evidence)
- Contributing factors (process, monitoring, testing gaps)
- Mitigation & remediation (short-term and long-term fixes) with owners and ETA
- Lessons learned and follow-ups
- Severity classification and whether credits/refunds are required

On-call rotations and shift succession guidance

- Rotation length: 2 weeks primary, followed by 1 week light rotation (observer) for handover and mentoring.
- Hand-over checklist (outgoing -> incoming):
  1. Current on-call incidents and status (link to active incident page).
  2. Calendar blocks for bridges or follow-ups.
  3. Known noisy alerts and suppression rules applied.
  4. PagerDuty escalation overrides active.
- Timezone considerations: ensure at least two responders overlap for cross-region incidents (prefer 1 hour overlap between EMEA and US shifts).
- On-call fatigue policy: mandatory 48-hour cool-down after a P0 incident for the primary responder; additional compensatory time-off tracked with People Ops.

Game-day syllabus and exercises

Purpose: Validate the Incident Keeper runloop and reduce cognitive load during real incidents. Schedule game days quarterly and after any major architecture change.

Exercise types:
- Silent-degradation drill: simulate p95 latency regression for a single region; tests monitoring, paging, and runbook accuracy.
- Thundering-neighbor: simulate noisy consumer causing autoscaling churn; tests throttles and capacity throttling strategies.
- KV cache OOM scenario: simulate memory leak in worker process; tests restart and cache-invalidation playbooks.
- Multi-zone failover: region outage simulation requiring traffic routing to other regions and validating data consistency.

Sample game day timeline (4 hours)
- 00:00 - 00:20: Orientation and objectives
- 00:20 - 01:00: Inject Scenario 1 (silent-degradation); observers collect timeline metrics
- 01:00 - 01:30: Remediation and verification for Scenario 1
- 01:30 - 02:15: Inject Scenario 2 (thundering neighbor)
- 02:15 - 03:00: Remediation and a simulated customer comms run
- 03:00 - 04:00: Hot retro and action item triage (assign owners within 48 hours)

Status page and customer communications templates

Public status page (initial post) — short and action-focused:

Title: "Partial outage impacting Redwood inference API (region: us-west)"
Posted: {{timestamp}}
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors or latency in us-west. We are actively investigating and will provide updates every 20 minutes.
What we are doing: Our operations team has opened a full incident bridge and is rolling back a recent deployment while validating traffic.
Suggested workaround: Route traffic to us-east or eu-central where possible. Contact support if you have a mission-critical workflow.

Customer internal update (20 minute cadence) — Slack/email template:

Subject: "Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — update: investigation ongoing (20:00 UTC)"
Body: "Scope: ~12% of requests in us-west returning 5xx. Actions taken: rollback initiated, worker concurrency reduced. Current status: partial stabilization observed — error-rate dropped from 18% -> 9% in the last 5 minutes. Next update at 20:20 UTC. Contact: support@redwood.ai or oncall pager."

Final resolution message (public):

Title: "Resolved — Redwood inference API"
Posted: {{timestamp}}
Status: Resolved
Summary: The incident impacting the us-west region has been resolved. Root cause: a canary deployment introduced an interaction between request batching and KV cache eviction which caused elevated 5xx rates. Mitigation: the deployment was rolled back; a safe-deploy guard will be added to the pipeline.
Customer impact: Customers may have experienced failed requests between 19:40 - 20:20 UTC. We are contacting high-touch customers directly with compensation where appropriate.

Example internal short status (Slack #incidents) — copy/paste:

[INCIDENT-1234] P0 us-west API outage — rollback complete; 5xx rate down from 18% -> 1.2% in 10m. Bridge: <link>. Next: validate synthetic checks, prepare final resolution by 20:40 UTC.

Training and runbook ownership

- Owners: Each runbook has a single named owner (Service Owner) and a secondary owner. Owners must review their runbooks quarterly and after every P1/P0 incident.
- Runbook QA: Runbooks must include: required dashboards, PromQL queries, sample commands, rollback instructions, and contact list. Missing sections will return the runbook to the owner as part of runbook-governance.

Appendix: Quick PromQL snippets (copy-paste)

- 5xx rate across API (last 5m):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-proxy",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-proxy"}[5m]))

- p95 latency for generation endpoint (1m window):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="gen"}[1m])) by (le))

- Pod restarts in last 15m:
  sum(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="prod"} - kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="prod"}[15m]) by (pod)

Contact and ownership

- On-call rotation manager: Ajay Singh (eng-sre)
- Incident Keeper rotation calendar: https://calendar.redwood.ai/oncall (internal)
- Questions/requests for runbook changes: runbooks@redwood.ai

Document maintenance

This page is owned by the Engineering SRE team. Review cadence: annual (or after any P0). Any edits require at least one reviewer from Eng SRE and one from Product before publishing.
